newsitem.title: GREECE: Tonnes of uncollected garbage choke Athens.
newsitem.headline: Tonnes of uncollected garbage choke Athens.

text.p: A six-day strike by municipal workers has left some 7,500 tonnes of uncollected garbage in the streets of Athens, festering in sweltering heat and threatening public health, officials said on Friday.
Athenians and thousands of tourists must dodge mountains of rotting garbage piled up in streets and pavements, outside cafes and even at the entrances of museums and archaeological sites.
The municipal workers are demanding that some 100 of their colleagues with temporary contracts are hired on a permanent basis and have shut down Athens' main garbage dump.
Health ministry officials warned of health risks from mounds of uncollected garbage, whose rise has matched that of the temperature, which has climbed as high as 30 degrees Celsius in the past week.
The workers were expected to decide later on Friday whether they would continue their action next week.
